title: Event Hire Storage in Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Unit ideas for party furniture, bouncy castle, photo booth, sound and marquee hire businesses in Blackpool. Units from £65 a week with 24-hour access.
lead: Hire businesses live and die by how fast they can load the van. A unit gives your chairs, inflatables, booths and speakers a dry, organised home between bookings, with lighting, electricity and Wi-Fi already connected and 24-hour access for early set-ups and late returns. Most of the year your stock is waiting for the next booking, so where it waits matters more than you might expect.
why: Most hire kit is wood, metal, fabric, vinyl and boxed electronics: bulky but low-risk, which is exactly what our units are set up for.
Roller-shutter access on the 150, 180 and 300 sq ft units means stacked chairs, trolleys and rolled inflatables go straight from the van to the shelf.

Weddings, parties and corporate events run early and finish late, so 24-hour access means you never wait for someone to open up after a midnight pack-down. Everything in one place also makes stocktakes and insurance lists far simpler.
uses: Party furniture hire

Folding chairs, trestle tables, chair covers and dance-floor-friendly furniture for weddings, christenings and garden parties. Stackable furniture takes less room than you might think, so a 180 sq ft unit holds a good stock for a small hire business. As bookings grow, you can add an adjoining unit rather than moving everything, subject to availability.
Stack chairs on wheeled dollies in rows along the back wall and stand tables on their sides in racks. Keep a clear lane from the shutter so a whole order can be wheeled out in one run.
Count every item out and back in on a simple checklist for each booking. Damage and shortfalls are much easier to charge for when you spot them on the day.
Bouncy castle and soft play hire

Inflatables, blowers, groundsheets, crash mats and soft play blocks for children's parties and community fun days. A dry unit protects vinyl from damp between bookings, which helps it last. Separate sets of mats and blocks by age group so the right kit goes to the right party.

Rolled inflatables on low pallets or heavy-duty shelving, blowers and extension leads on a shelf above, and soft play pieces stacked by colour or set. Leave floor space near the shutter for drying and checking returns.
Make sure an inflatable is fully dry before it goes back in storage, or it can mould. Look up the HSE guidance on inflatables and the PIPA testing scheme so your kit is inspected and safe to hire.
Photo booth and selfie mirror hire

Enclosed booths, magic mirrors, printers, props boxes and backdrops for weddings, proms and corporate events. The 160 sq ft unit with a security door suits this compact, high-value kit. Software, card readers and templates can all be prepared at the unit on the Wi-Fi.

Booths in flight cases or on trolleys along one wall, a bench with power and Wi-Fi for updating software and templates, and props sorted into themed boxes. Keep spare printer paper and ink sealed on a shelf.
Test each booth and its printer in the unit before it goes out. A quick check the day before saves a panicked fix in front of a wedding party.
DJ, sound and lighting hire

PA speakers, mixers, microphones, LED uplighters, dance floor lighting and stands for DJs, bands and events that hire their own production kit. Store everything in flight cases and you can stack it safely to the ceiling. Keeping kit in one place also makes it easier to PAT test and log your hire stock.
Flight cases on low shelving with heavy speakers at the bottom, cables coiled and labelled in crates, and a test bench with plenty of sockets. Keep a shelf for kit waiting to be checked or repaired.
Standard single-phase power is fine for testing PA and lighting kit. Do not store smoke or haze machine fluid in bulk, and ask us before bringing in anything flammable.
Marquee and gazebo hire

Pop-up gazebos, frame marquees, sidewalls, weights, flooring and pegs for garden parties, markets and outdoor events. Poles and canvas are low-risk, and a roller-shutter unit makes long frames easy to load. Many outdoor event businesses pair marquees with furniture hire from the same unit.

Poles and frames in long racks against one wall, canvas and sidewalls folded and bagged on shelving, and weights and pegs in crates at floor level. Label every bag with the size of marquee it belongs to.
Dry canvas fully before storing it, even if that means spreading it out on the unit floor for an evening. Patio heaters that run on gas cylinders are not allowed in the unit.
Garden games and giant games hire

Giant Jenga, Connect 4, quoits, croquet sets, lawn bowls and table football for weddings, pub events and summer fetes. Wooden games are light, low-risk and easy to stack in labelled boxes. They are also an easy add-on to sell alongside furniture or marquee bookings.
Games in labelled crates on shelving, bigger frames such as giant Connect 4 standing upright, and a packing table for counting pieces. Keep a box of spare blocks and pegs for quick swaps.
Count pieces back in after each hire and sand or replace damaged wooden blocks straight away. A tidy set looks better in photos and earns repeat bookings.
faqs: Can I store a generator for events?

Petrol and diesel fuel are not allowed in the units, and nor are gas cylinders unless we have agreed it in writing. If you hire out generators, ask us on WhatsApp before you commit so we can talk it through.
Which unit is best for a hire business?

For bulky stock such as furniture, inflatables or marquees, the 180 sq ft roller-shutter unit or the 300 sq ft two-storey unit work well. Compact kit such as photo booths suits the 160 sq ft security-door unit.
I already store wedding decorations. Is that a different page?
Event styling props such as arches, backdrops and centrepieces are covered on our trades and business storage ideas. This page is for businesses that hire out kit. Many do both from one unit.

title: Storage for Market Traders, Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Unit ideas for market stall holders, craft fair sellers, antiques dealers and seasonal traders in Blackpool. Store stock and stall kit from £65 a week.
lead: Trading at markets and fairs means packing a whole shop into a van and back out again, often before sunrise. A unit gives your stock, gazebo and trestles a permanent home near central Blackpool, so your house and garage stop being the warehouse. Lighting, electricity and Wi-Fi are already connected, so you can price stock and do the books there too.
why: Market stock is mostly boxed goods, clothing, homeware, crafts and collectables: dry, low-risk items that sit well on shelving in our units.
24-hour access matters when a market sets up at dawn or a fair finishes late, and a roller shutter means the gazebo, weights and crates go in quickly.

Rolling monthly terms suit a trade that changes with the seasons, and you can swap to a bigger or smaller unit when your stock grows or shrinks, subject to availability. A tidy stockroom means quicker set-ups and less time standing in the cold on market mornings.
uses: Market stall kit and stock base

Your gazebo, trestle tables, weights, display stands, cloths and stock crates kept in one place, packed and ready for the next market day. Many traders find a 150 sq ft unit holds a full stall plus a few weeks of stock. It also means you can restock mid-week without unpacking the van in your drive.

Stall kit together in one corner nearest the shutter, stock on shelving in labelled crates behind it, and a packing table for building the next day's load. Keep a written list of what goes in the van so nothing is left behind.
Load the van the night before using your 24-hour access, then you only have to drive and set up in the morning.
Craft fair and makers' market sellers

For makers who sell at craft fairs, Christmas markets and pop-up events: finished stock, display props, card readers and packaging in one tidy stockroom. You can also price, bag and tag stock at a proper table instead of the kitchen. Between fairs, the same space works as a stockroom for online sales.

Finished stock in clear boxes by product line, display props and risers on a separate shelf, and a pricing and packing table under good light. Keep a small grab box of float, bags, tape and spare price labels.
Take a photo of a well-laid-out stall and stick it on the wall. It makes setting up at the next fair quicker and more consistent.
Antiques and collectables dealer

Furniture, ceramics, prints, militaria, toys and collectables bought at auctions and house sales, cleaned and priced before they go to antiques fairs or online. A two-storey unit lets you keep bulky pieces downstairs and smaller valuable items upstairs. Buyers and other dealers can visit you at the unit by arrangement.

Larger furniture on the ground floor with walkways between pieces, fragile items on deep shelving with padding, and a cleaning and pricing bench. Keep stock you are researching separate from stock that is ready to sell.
Wrap fragile pieces in paper or blankets, not plastic that traps moisture. Keep a simple stock book with what you paid, where it came from and where it sold.
Seasonal and Christmas market stock

Christmas decorations, gifts, calendars, Halloween stock and summer seaside goods bought in bulk ahead of the season and sold over a few busy weeks. A unit lets you buy early at better prices and store it until it is needed. When the season ends, stock that did not sell can be boxed up for next year.

Stock for the current season at the front, next season's stock boxed and labelled at the back, and shelving high enough to use the full wall. Leave a clear area by the shutter for deliveries arriving.
Rolling monthly terms mean you can take a bigger unit for the busy months and drop back down afterwards, subject to availability.
House clearance resale

Sorting goods from house clearances into stock for markets, car boot sales and online listings. Clothes, books, homeware and furniture can all be sorted, cleaned and priced in one place. Many clearance traders sell the best pieces online and the rest on markets.

Three clear zones: an intake area by the shutter, a sorting and cleaning table in the middle, and shelving for priced stock. Keep a separate area for items going to charity or the tip so they leave quickly.
Check what comes in before it goes on the shelves. Fuel cans, paint tins, aerosols in quantity and gas bottles from clearances cannot be stored in the unit.
Gift, jewellery and accessories stall

Small, high-value lines such as costume jewellery, phone accessories, sunglasses, bags and gifts that sell well on markets and at seaside events. The 160 sq ft security-door unit suits stock that is small but worth a lot. Wi-Fi at the unit makes reordering from suppliers quick between market days.

Stock in drawer units or small labelled bins, display cards and stands boxed by stall layout, and a desk for reordering and bookkeeping on the Wi-Fi. Keep the most valuable lines in a lockable cabinet.
Count small stock in and out each market day. It is the quickest way to spot theft at the stall and to know which lines are worth reordering.
faqs: Can I load my van at any time?
Yes. Tenants have 24-hour access, so you can load the night before or come back late after a market. Vehicles cannot be stored inside the units, as car storage is not permitted.
Do I need a licence to trade at markets?

Most markets and fairs handle pitch bookings themselves, and some street trading needs a council licence. Check with the market organiser and Blackpool Council. Our guide to selling at Blackpool markets covers the basics.
Can I store food stock for my stall?
Cooking and hot food are not allowed. Some dry, pre-packed food may be possible, but ask us first, and check the Food Standards Agency guidance on registering a food business with your council.

title: Furniture Upcycling Workshop, Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Workshop ideas for furniture painters, upholsterers, restorers and reclaimed wood makers in Blackpool. Units from £65 a week, water-based paints only.
lead: Upcycling takes space: a piece waiting to be stripped, one drying, one ready for collection and a stack of finds from the last auction. A unit gives you a proper workshop with lighting, electricity and Wi-Fi already connected, room to leave work in progress and a place for customers to collect. Water-based paints only: no solvent spraying.
why: Wood, fabric, hand tools and water-based paints are low-risk, which fits our rules. Solvent spraying and solvent-based finishes are not allowed.
Roller-shutter units make it easy to bring in a wardrobe or a sideboard, and the 300 sq ft two-storey unit gives you an upstairs area with a window for admin, small pieces or photography.

You can receive customers at the unit to view finished pieces or drop off furniture for repair, and use the address on your Google Business Profile. Clear wood dust regularly and keep the area around heaters and sockets free of shavings and rags.
uses: Painted furniture upcycling

Transforming chests of drawers, sideboards, tables and chairs with chalk-style, mineral and other water-based paints, brushed or rollered on. Water-based paints and finishes only: no solvent paints and no spray guns using solvents. A steady supply of auction and charity shop finds means you always have the next piece ready to start.

A prep area for cleaning and sanding near the shutter, a painting area on dust sheets in the middle, and a drying zone at the back where pieces will not be knocked. Keep paints on a shelf with lids on. Label each piece with its customer or sale status so nothing gets sold or painted by mistake.
Use a dust extractor or vacuum with your sander and sweep up daily. Very old furniture may have lead paint, so read the HSE guidance before sanding anything you are unsure about.
Reupholstery workshop

Re-covering dining chairs, footstools, headboards and occasional chairs with webbing, hessian, wadding and fabric using hand tools and a staple gun. Customers can drop off and collect at the unit. Keeping customers' chairs out of your home also looks more professional.

A sturdy padded work trestle in the centre, fabric rolls on a wall rack, tools on a pegboard, and a shelf for customers' pieces labelled with name and job. Keep fabric samples near the door for consultations.
Fabric, webbing and wadding are low-risk materials. Ask us before bringing in large quantities of foam or spray adhesives.
Furniture repair and restoration

Regluing loose joints, replacing drawer runners, patching veneer, fixing handles and refreshing finishes on antique and everyday furniture. Small repairs for local customers can be a steady trade alongside upcycling. Restoration work often comes through word of mouth once people know where to find you.

A solid workbench with a vice and clamps, timber offcuts and spare hardware in labelled drawers, and a finishing bench kept as dust-free as you can. Store customers' items under covers. Keep a box of salvaged handles, hinges and knobs: they are often the hardest parts to match.
Choose water-based glues, stains and lacquers. Ask us before using any solvent-based product, even in small amounts.
Reclaimed wood and pallet furniture

Building benches, shelves, coffee tables, planters and headboards from reclaimed timber, scaffold boards and pallets. Wood is a low-risk material, and a roller shutter makes long boards easy to bring in. Commissions for made-to-measure pieces are a good way to fill quiet weeks.
Timber stored flat on a wall rack sorted by length, a cutting station with a mitre saw and dust collection, and an assembly bench. Keep finished pieces wrapped near the shutter for delivery.
Check reclaimed timber for nails and screws before cutting. Clear offcuts and sawdust regularly, and never leave a pile of shavings by a heater.
Upcycled furniture showroom by appointment

Show finished pieces to buyers by appointment, photograph stock for online listings and run the business from the upstairs room with a window. Customers can view and collect at the unit. Viewings by appointment work well alongside selling through online marketplaces.

Finished, styled pieces on the ground floor arranged like a small room, a photo corner with a plain backdrop and good lights, and the office upstairs for admin and calls. Keep work in progress separate from stock for sale. Change the room set every few weeks so returning buyers always see something new.
The ground floor is windowless, so add warm lamps to show pieces at their best. Good photos sell upcycled furniture as much as the piece itself.
Small homeware and mirror upcycling

Revamping mirrors, picture frames, lamps, trays, stools and bedside tables that sell well online and at craft fairs. Small pieces mean you can work in a compact unit and sell in volume. These pieces also make good stock for markets and gift fairs.
Benches along two walls, one for prep and one for painting, a drying rack for small items, and boxed stock on shelving. A packing table helps if you post pieces to online buyers.
If you rewire lamps for sale, have them checked by a qualified electrician. Selling electrical goods comes with safety responsibilities, so check the official guidance before you start.
faqs: Can I spray-paint furniture in the unit?

No solvent spraying. Water-based paints, stains and finishes applied by brush, roller or cloth are fine. Solvent-based paints and chemicals in bulk are not allowed unless we have agreed it in writing.
Is there space to dry painted furniture?

Yes, if you plan for it. Keep a drying zone at the back of the unit away from the door. For bigger pieces or more stock, the 180 sq ft roller-shutter unit or the 300 sq ft two-storey unit give you more room.
Can I run power tools such as sanders and saws?

Benchtop and hand-held power tools for wood are generally fine on standard single-phase electricity. Use dust extraction and tell us what you plan to use when you enquire. Our guide to setting up a small workshop has more tips.

title: Storage for Gardeners, Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Unit ideas for gardeners, landscapers, garden designers and tree surgeons in Blackpool. Store tools and materials from £65 a week, 24-hour access.
lead: Gardening businesses carry a lot of kit, and a van full of tools overnight is a target. A unit gives your mowers, trimmers, materials and paperwork a secure home, with lighting, electricity for charging and Wi-Fi already connected, and 24-hour access for early starts. Winter is a good time to set up, so you are organised before the spring rush.
why: Battery and electric tools, hand tools, timber, fencing and bagged materials are low-risk to store. Petrol tools stored with fuel and fuel cans are not allowed.
Electricity is connected in every unit, so you can charge a full set of battery tools overnight ready for the next day's work.

Roller-shutter access makes it easy to wheel mowers in and out, and 24-hour access means you can load up before the first job of the day. Keeping the floor swept of soil and grass clippings also keeps the unit pleasant to work in.
uses: Gardener's battery tool base

Battery mowers, strimmers, hedge trimmers, blowers and hand tools stored and charged in one place for a garden maintenance round. Many gardeners have switched to battery kit, and it suits a unit perfectly. It also keeps muddy kit out of the van cab and out of your garage at home.

A charging shelf with batteries spaced apart near the sockets, mowers parked in a line by the shutter, and long-handled tools in wall racks. Keep a bench for cleaning blades and sharpening. A hook for each tool makes it obvious at the end of the day if something has been left on a job.
Charge batteries while you are around and unplug them when they are full. Petrol mowers and tools cannot be stored with fuel in them, and fuel cans are not allowed.
Landscaping materials store

Fence panels, posts, sleepers, decking boards, edging, membrane and bagged products for landscaping jobs. Buying in bulk and storing it can save money and trips to the merchant. Holding materials at the unit means you can start a job the day it is confirmed.

Long timber stacked flat on bearers against the back wall, bagged materials on pallets, and smaller fixings in labelled bins. Keep the route from the shutter clear so the heaviest items load last. A whiteboard listing stock and jobs it is earmarked for stops materials being used twice.
Do not overload shelving with heavy bags, and stack sleepers safely. Ask us before storing large amounts of loose aggregate or anything that could make a mess of the floor.
Garden design studio

A ground floor for sample boards, plant lists and material samples, with the upstairs room with a window as a studio for drawing plans and meeting clients. A proper base looks professional when clients visit. Design work fits naturally alongside a maintenance round or a landscaping crew.

Paving and cladding samples displayed on the ground floor, a large table for laying out plans, and a desk upstairs with good light. Keep past project photos on a screen or in a portfolio. Keep a small plant reference library and catalogues on a shelf by the table.
Clients can visit the unit. You can also use the address on your Google Business Profile instead of your home.
Tree surgery and hedge cutting kit

Climbing ropes, harnesses, helmets, battery chainsaws, pole saws, ladders and PPE stored dry and checked between jobs. Keeping climbing kit in one dry place makes inspections easier. A dedicated store makes it easier to keep inspection records up to date.

Ropes and harnesses hung on hooks off the floor, ladders on wall brackets, saws in cases on a shelf, and an inspection bench with a log book. Keep wet kit on a drying rack, not in a heap. Separate PPE that needs replacing so it never goes back out by mistake.
Petrol chainsaws must not be stored with fuel, and fuel cans are not allowed. Check HSE guidance on chainsaw work and on inspecting climbing equipment.
Wreaths and seasonal garden decor

Making Christmas wreaths, door swags and dried flower arrangements in the run-up to the holidays, plus spring and summer planters for sale. It is a good way to keep a gardening business earning in winter. Workshops teaching wreath making can work too, if you tell us numbers in advance.
A long making table, foliage and moss in crates on the floor, bases and ribbons on shelving, and finished wreaths hung on a rail. Keep a clear area by the door for collections.
Fresh foliage and dried flowers are fine. Glue guns melt plastic, so ask us before using one, and wire your wreaths instead where you can.
Pots, planters and garden accessories stock

Stock of pots, planters, bird feeders, garden ornaments and tools for selling online, at markets or to your own maintenance customers. Store it in winter when prices are low and sell through spring. Offering pots and planters to your existing customers is an easy extra sale.

Heavy pots on the floor or bottom shelves, lighter items up high, and a packing area for online orders. Wrap ceramics in paper before stacking. A small display shelf near the door works well if customers collect orders.
Plants need daylight, and the ground floors are windowless, so store hard goods here and keep live plants somewhere bright.
faqs: Can I store a petrol mower in the unit?

Not with fuel in it, and fuel cans are not allowed. Flammable liquids are not permitted in bulk. Battery and electric tools are the easiest choice. If you have a particular machine in mind, ask us on WhatsApp.
Can I charge my battery tools in the unit?
Yes. Electricity is connected in every unit, and usage is charged separately at the supplier rate with no markup. Charge batteries while you are around and do not leave damaged batteries in the unit.
Which unit suits a gardening business?
A 150 sq ft roller-shutter unit holds tools and mowers for a one-person round. For materials and bigger kit, look at the 180 sq ft unit, or the two-storey unit if you also want an office.

title: Storage for Clubs and Groups, Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Unit ideas for sports clubs, scout groups, drama societies, bands, charities and hobby clubs in Blackpool. Shared kit storage from £65 a week.
lead: Club kit tends to end up in someone's garage, which works until that person moves, falls out or goes on holiday. A shared unit gives your group one place for everything, with 24-hour access so volunteers can collect kit when it suits them. Lighting and electricity are already connected, and costs can be shared across the group.
why: Sports kit, tents, props, costumes and instruments are low-risk to store, and every unit has lighting and electricity already connected.
24-hour access suits volunteers who can only collect kit before work, after training or at weekends.

Rolling monthly terms with one month's notice suit groups that need to keep costs predictable and might change plans at the AGM. A short note on the wall with the group's contact details helps if anything needs sorting.
uses: Sports club kit store

Goals, nets, balls, cones, bibs, first aid kits and match kit for junior football, rugby, cricket or netball clubs. One place for kit means less chasing round on match day. Clubs often find it easier to grow once the kit has a proper home.

Nets and portable goals in a rack by the shutter, balls in mesh bags on hooks, kit in labelled crates by team, and a shelf for first aid. Put a list of every team's kit on the wall. Colour-coded crates for each age group stop kit drifting between teams over the season.
Let kit dry fully before it goes back in, or the unit will smell by spring. Choose a named person to look after the key and the check-out list.
Scout, guide and youth group camping kit

Patrol tents, groundsheets, cooking kit, tables, lanterns, ropes and activity equipment for scout, guide and youth groups. A dry unit helps canvas and kit last longer. Leaders can collect kit for weekend camps without relying on one person's garage.

Tents bagged and labelled on deep shelving, poles in a long rack, activity kit in crates, and a drying area near the shutter after camp. Keep a kit list for each camp. Store small items such as mallets, pegs and lanterns in clear tubs so leaders can see at a glance what is missing.
Gas cylinders and camping gas cannot be stored in the unit unless we have agreed it in writing, so keep stoves without their gas. Dry tents fully before storing them.
Amateur dramatics props and scenery

Flats, props, costumes, furniture and set pieces for drama groups, panto societies and school productions. Blackpool has a strong theatre tradition, and kit builds up quickly. Shared rails and labelled boxes also make it easy to lend kit to other groups.

Scenery flats standing upright in racks, costumes on rails in garment bags, props in boxes labelled by production, and furniture covered at the back. The upstairs of a two-storey unit works well for costumes. A rail of costumes sorted by size saves hours at casting and dress rehearsals.
Paint scenery with water-based paints only. Keep a photo index of props so directors can choose without opening every box.
Band and PA equipment storage

Drums, amplifiers, PA speakers, stands and cables for bands, choirs and community music groups that play in different venues. Flight cases stack well in a small unit. It keeps expensive equipment out of members' cars and homes between gigs.

Heavy amps and speakers low down, drums in cases on a shelf, and cables coiled in labelled crates. Keep a test bench with sockets for checking kit before a gig. Mark each case with the band's name and a contact number in case anything goes astray at a venue.
Ask us before using the unit for rehearsals, because sound carries in a shared building. Storage and kit maintenance are the easy part.
Charity donations sorting

Sorting donated clothes, books, toys and homeware for a charity shop, appeal or community swap. A unit keeps donations dry and organised before they go out. Volunteers can work in shifts, with 24-hour access fitting around their jobs.

An intake area by the shutter, sorting tables in the middle, and shelving for sorted stock by type. Keep a clear area for bags going to recycling so they do not build up. Labelled bags for each type of donation make the next sorting session far quicker for volunteers.
Check donations as they come in. Aerosols in quantity, paint, fuel and gas bottles cannot be stored, and cooked or fresh food is not allowed.
Hobby club room

A base for a model railway, wargaming, board game or radio club where members can leave layouts and projects set up. Members can meet at the unit, with shared toilets and a tea and coffee room on site. Having a permanent room is often what keeps a club going year after year.

Layouts or gaming tables in the centre, storage around the edges, and a bench with good lighting for modelling. In the two-storey unit, use the upstairs room with a window for meetings. Folding tables and stackable chairs mean you can clear the floor when you need room for a bigger meeting.
Tell us how many people you expect at a session so we can check it suits the space. Ask before fixing anything to the walls.
faqs: Can a club or charity rent a unit?

Yes, subject to our approval of the use. Someone needs to sign up with valid government-issued photo ID and a Direct Debit mandate, with one month's rent in advance and a deposit. See our rental terms for the details.
Can more than one member have access?
Ask us on WhatsApp how access works for groups. Most groups name one or two people as the key contacts and keep a simple check-out list for kit.
Which unit suits a small club?
For balls, nets and bibs, a 150 sq ft roller-shutter unit is often enough. For tents or scenery, look at the 180 sq ft unit or the 300 sq ft two-storey unit.

title: Storage for Mobile Businesses, Blackpool | The Rock Factory
desc: Kit and stock storage in Blackpool for mobile hairdressers, dog groomers, valeters, nail techs and therapists. Units from £65 a week, 24-hour access.
lead: When your business runs from a van or a car boot, stock and spare kit end up all over the house. A unit gives you a base to store kit, restock between appointments and do your admin, with lighting, electricity and Wi-Fi already connected. Services are carried out at your customers' homes, not in the unit, unless we have approved it. Many mobile businesses find a base also helps keep work and home life separate.
why: Most mobile kit is tools, towels, boxed products and small equipment: low-risk items that store well on shelving.
24-hour access lets you restock before an early first appointment or drop kit back after a late one.

You can use the address on your Google Business Profile, which keeps your home address off the internet while showing customers you are a local business. Keep a simple list of what you store at the unit and what lives on the van.
uses: Mobile hairdresser and barber stockroom

Colour, shampoo, styling products, towels, capes, dryers and spare tools kept in one place, with a desk for bookings and accounts. Buying products in bulk is cheaper when you have somewhere to keep them. A unit also gives you somewhere quiet to do your accounts and plan your rounds.

Products on shelving sorted by brand and shade, clean and used towels in separate labelled bins, and a bench where you pack your kit bag for the day. Keep a stock list so you reorder before you run out.
Store products in everyday quantities and keep aerosols to a sensible number. Appointments happen at clients' homes; ask us before seeing any clients in the unit.
Mobile dog grooming kit store

Grooming tables, dryers, clippers, blades, shampoos, towels and spare parts for a mobile dog groomer. Keeping spares at the unit means a broken clipper does not end your day. Spare kit at the unit is also handy when you take on a second groomer or van.

Spare tables and dryers along one wall, clipper blades and tools in drawers, shampoo stock on shelving, and a clean bench for servicing kit. Keep wet towels separate until they go home to wash. A wall chart of blade sizes and sharpening dates keeps the kit in good order.
Grooming dogs in the unit is not allowed unless we have approved it. This is a base for storing and preparing kit, with services carried out in your van or at customers' homes.
Car valeting and detailing supplies

Cleaning products, polishes, microfibre cloths, vacuums, pressure washers and water tanks for a mobile valeter or detailer. Bulk products and spare kit stay at the unit, and the van carries only what you need. It is easier to keep products organised when the van is not doing double duty as a warehouse.
Products on low shelving in original containers, machines along one wall, cloths in labelled crates, and a bench for servicing pressure washers. Keep a clear route from the shutter to load the van.
No vehicles can be stored or valeted in the unit. Keep products to everyday quantities and ask us before storing anything flammable or solvent-based.
Mobile nail technician and beauty therapist

Polishes, gels, lamps, files, towels, wax products and portable couches for a mobile nail or beauty business. A tidy stockroom makes it quick to pack the right kit for each client. A tidy base also makes it easier to keep on top of hygiene and stock rotation.

Products in clear drawers by type and colour, portable couches and chairs stored upright, and a desk for bookings, ordering and social media. Keep clean linen in sealed boxes. A small labelled kit bag per treatment type makes packing for the day quick.
Nail polish, acetone and similar products are flammable, so keep only small, everyday amounts in their original bottles. Treatments happen at clients' homes unless we have approved otherwise.
Mobile massage and sports therapy

Massage couches, bolsters, linen, oils, supports and rehab equipment for a therapist who visits clients, sports clubs and events. A unit keeps clean linen and kit organised and away from the family home. Event and club work often means carrying extra couches and kit, which the unit can hold.
Couches standing upright in their bags, clean linen on shelving, used linen in lidded bins, and a desk for treatment notes. Keep client records locked away or on a secure device.
Store massage oils in small bottles in everyday quantities. Client notes are personal data, so check the ICO guidance on keeping records secure.
Window cleaning round base

Water-fed poles, hoses, ladders, buckets, squeegees and filter equipment for a window cleaning round. Long poles and ladders are much easier to store in a unit than at home. The 300 sq ft unit suits a round with two vans and a small office upstairs.

Poles and ladders in long wall racks, hoses on reels, small tools in crates by the shutter, and a bench for repairs. Keep the floor clear so you can load the van quickly in the morning. Hang a checklist by the shutter so you never leave for a round without a key piece of kit.
Water is available in the shared facilities, but ask us before planning to fill van tanks or run a filter system at the unit.
faqs: Can I see clients in my unit?

Tenants can receive clients at the unit, but treatments and services such as grooming, hairdressing and beauty need our approval first. Most mobile businesses use the unit for storage, restocking and admin, and carry out the work at customers' homes.
Can I park or store my van in the unit?
No. Car and vehicle storage is not permitted because of the buildings insurance. The unit is for your kit, products and paperwork.
Which unit suits a mobile business?

A 150 sq ft roller-shutter unit or the 160 sq ft security-door unit suits most kit and stock. For long poles or bulky machines, try the 180 sq ft unit. Also see our guide to using a business address on Google.
